udt_struct_v0.doc: A public, on-chain record that a fact was proven from a DKIM-signed email.\nStored keyed by `nullifier` \xe2\x80\x94 this is exactly what the public page /p/:id reads.\nIt holds NO email contents: only commitments. Revealing it leaks nothing.
udt_struct_v0.name: Attestation

fields.name: nullifier

fields.doc: domain-separated sha256 of the proven statement (public signals EXCEPT the\nnullifier) \xe2\x80\x94 commits to the fact, recomputable by the frontend from link metadata

fields.name: timestamp

function_v0.doc: Whether an email/proof carrying this nullifier has already been sealed.
function_v0.name: is_sealed

function_v0.doc:
Verify a proof AND seal it as a public attestation.

This is the real entry point. Order matters:
1. the proof must verify \xe2\x80\x94 that is what makes `pub_signals` trustworthy
(a valid proof cryptographically binds them; they are not free input);
2. the nullifier (pub_signals[0], bound by the circuit to the email's DKIM
signature) must be unseen \xe2\x80\x94 otherwise the SAME email is being replayed;
3. only then do we persist the attestation and emit an event.

Returns the attestation id (== the nullifier) used by the public /p/:id page.
function_v0.name: submit_proof

function_v0.doc: Pure verification: is `proof` valid for `pub_signals` under the embedded VK?\nRead-only, changes no state. Useful for clients/tests; the real flow is\n`submit_proof`, which also seals the result.
function_v0.name: verify_proof

function_v0.doc: Read a sealed attestation by id (== nullifier). Powers the public /p/:id page\nwith REAL on-chain state. Returns None if nothing was sealed under that id.
function_v0.name: get_attestation
